To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) the human kinome is highly interconnected, and (ii) the kinome is highly phosphorylated and the phospho-proteins interact with each other and with other proteins.

1) The human phosphoproteome is a highly connected network of 20,000 proteins, 500 kinases and 30,000 sites, 2) the network is organized into 10 distinct sub-networks, each with a characteristic set of proteins, kinases and sites, and 3) the sub-networks can be classified into 5 major categories based on the biological function of their proteins.

PhosphoPOINT is a human kinase interactome that provides information about the substrates and phosphorylation sites of kinases, as well as information about the kinases that phosphorylate these sites.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we are able to predict phosphorylation sites with high accuracy, even when the kinase is unknown and only the protein sequence is available.
the phosphoPOINT database can be used to identify the most likely kinases responsible for phosphorylation events of interest and to identify the most relevant phospho-sites for a given kinase.
we have created a comprehensive human kinase and phospho-proteome interactome.
